title: Iwahori-Weyl Group
body_html:
Iwahori-Weyl Group

The Iwahori-Weyl group \(\widetilde{W}\) is the group of symmetries of the Bruhat-Tits building that preserves the apartment. It governs the Bruhat decomposition relative to an Iwahori subgroup and is the natural group for the affine Hecke algebra.

Setup

Let \(G\) be a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field \(F\) with Henselian valuation \(\omega : F^\times \to \mathbb{Z}\). Fix a maximal \(F\)-split torus \(S \subseteq G\) with centralizer \(T = Z_G(S)\) (a maximal \(F\)-torus when \(G\) is quasi-split) and normalizer \(N = N_G(S)\).

The maximal bounded subgroup of \(T(F)\) is \[ T(F)_0 \;:=\; \{t \in T(F) : \omega(\chi(t)) = 0 \text{ for all } \chi \in X^*(T)\}. \] This equals \(T(\mathcal{O}_F)\) for the natural integral model of \(T\).

Definition

The Iwahori-Weyl group is the quotient \[ \widetilde{W} \;:=\; N(F) \big/ T(F)_0. \]

Structure

There is a canonical short exact sequence \[ 1 \;\to\; X_*(S) \;\to\; \widetilde{W} \;\to\; W_0 \;\to\; 1, \] where \(W_0 = N(F)/T(F)\) is the relative Weyl group of \((G, S)\). This sequence is split when \(G\) is split (in general it is a non-trivial extension when the derived group has non-trivial fundamental group).

The image of a cocharacter \(\mu \in X_*(S)\) in \(\widetilde{W}\) is the element \(t_\mu := \mu(\varpi)\, \mathrm{mod}\, T(F)_0\), where \(\varpi \in F^\times\) is a uniformiser. This is the translation element by \(\mu\).

When \(G\) is split, \(\widetilde{W} = X_*(T) \rtimes W_0\) as a semidirect product.

Comparison with affine Weyl group

The affine Weyl group is the subgroup \(W_{\mathrm{aff}} \subseteq \widetilde{W}\) generated by the affine reflections \(\{s_{\alpha, k} : \alpha \in \Phi, k \in \mathbb{Z}\}\) (reflection across the hyperplane \(\{\alpha = k\}\)). It is a normal subgroup: \[ W_{\mathrm{aff}} = X_*(T)_{\mathrm{coroot}} \rtimes W_0 \] where \(X_*(T)_{\mathrm{coroot}} \subseteq X_*(T)\) is the coroot lattice.

The Iwahori-Weyl group \(\widetilde{W}\) is generally larger than \(W_{\mathrm{aff}}\): \[ W_{\mathrm{aff}} \;\subseteq\; \widetilde{W}, \quad \widetilde{W} / W_{\mathrm{aff}} \;\cong\; X_*(T) / X_*(T)_{\mathrm{coroot}} \;\cong\; \pi_1(G_{\mathrm{sc}}), \] the algebraic fundamental group. The quotient is the extended affine Weyl group's component group, trivial for simply connected \(G\) and \(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}\) for \(\mathrm{PGL}_n\).

Bruhat decomposition

Theorem (Kaletha-Prasad §7.8). Let \(I \subseteq G(F)\) be an Iwahori subgroup (stabilizer of an alcove in \(\mathcal{B}(G,F)\)). Then \[ G(F) \;=\; \bigsqcup_{\tilde{w} \in \widetilde{W}} I\, \tilde{w}\, I, \] and this is a disjoint union. The map \(\tilde{w} \mapsto I\tilde{w}I\) is a bijection between \(\widetilde{W}\) and the double coset space \(I \backslash G(F) / I\).

Iwahori-Hecke algebra

The Iwahori-Hecke algebra is \[ \mathcal{H}(G(F), I) \;:=\; \mathcal{C}_c^\infty(I \backslash G(F) / I), \] with convolution product. By the Bruhat decomposition, \(\mathcal{H}(G(F), I)\) has a \(\mathbb{C}\)-basis \(\{T_{\tilde{w}} : \tilde{w} \in \widetilde{W}\}\) with structure constants determined by the length function \(\ell : \widetilde{W} \to \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\).

For simple reflections \(s \in W_{\mathrm{aff}}\), the Hecke operators satisfy \[ (T_s - q)(T_s + 1) = 0, \] where \(q = |\mathbb{F}_q|\) is the size of the residue field.

Examples

Group \(W_0\) \(\widetilde{W}\) \(W_{\mathrm{aff}}\)
\(\mathrm{SL}_2(F)\) \(\mathbb{Z}/2\) \(\mathbb{Z} \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/2\) (infinite dihedral) \(= \widetilde{W}\)
\(\mathrm{GL}_2(F)\) \(\mathbb{Z}/2\) \(\mathbb{Z}^2 \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/2\) index 1 in \(\widetilde{W}\)
\(\mathrm{PGL}_2(F)\) \(\mathbb{Z}/2\) \(\mathbb{Z} \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/2\) \(\widetilde{W}\) (same, since \(\pi_1 = \mathbb{Z}/2\) but cocharacter lattice quotient is \(\mathbb{Z}/2\))
\(\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\) \(S_n\) \(\mathbb{Z}^n \rtimes S_n\) \(\{(\mu, w) : \sum \mu_i = 0\} \rtimes S_n\)

Role in representation theory

  • The Bernstein-Zelevinsky decomposition of \(\mathrm{Rep}(G(F))\) has Bernstein components indexed by inertial classes; the Iwahori-Hecke algebra is the Hecke algebra of each component containing the unramified characters.
  • The Satake isomorphism identifies the spherical Hecke algebra (double cosets of a hyperspecial subgroup) with \(\mathbb{C}[X_*(T)]^{W_0}\), the representation ring of the Langlands dual group.
  • For \(\mathrm{GL}_n\), the Iwahori-Hecke algebra \(\mathcal{H}(G(F), I)\) is the affine Hecke algebra \(\mathcal{H}(n, q)\), whose specialization at \(q = 1\) gives \(\mathbb{C}[S_n]\) (degenerate affine Hecke).
